outcome: maternal transfusion >4 units of packed red blood cells (PRBCs)
need for conversion to general anesthesia (GETA)
cohort: Patients with pathologically confirmed Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) undergoing scheduled surgery at the study institution between September 2019 and November 2023, where the surgery was scheduled and the placenta was not entirely covering the anterior uterine wall.
finding: In appropriately selected patients, a transverse skin incision for PAS surgery was associated with significantly lower conversion to general anesthesia compared to a vertical incision, with equivalent rates of maternal transfusion and intraoperative complications.
